name: Japanese · Phrases · Shopping and paying
source: Phrases: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org) sentences written by native speakers, each linked in its src; lines marked generated were written for Lianki and checked for natural use

entries.reading: いらっしゃいませ
entries.note: Said by shop staff as you walk in — no reply needed.

entries.reading: みてるだけです
entries.note: When a clerk offers help and you only want to browse.

entries.reading: これいくらですか
entries.note: Point at the item; prices are usually marked, but not always at markets.

entries.term: 試着してもいいですか？
entries.reading: しちゃくしてもいいですか
entries.note: Ask before using the fitting room; staff may count your items.

entries.term: 色違いはありませんか？
entries.reading: いろちがいはありませんか
entries.back: Do you have this in other colours?
entries.note: Asking about the same item in a different colour.

entries.term: もう少し大きいサイズはありますか？
entries.reading: もうすこしおおきいサイズはありますか
entries.back: Do you have a bigger size?
entries.note: Swap in 小さい for smaller.

entries.reading: これにあう
entries.back: Does this look good on me?
entries.note: Asking a friend while shopping together.

entries.term: その眼鏡、よく似合ってるよ。
entries.reading: そのめがねよくにあってるよ
entries.note: Complimenting a friend; swap in 服, 帽子, 色…

entries.reading: どっちがいいとおもう
entries.back: Which one do you think is better?
entries.note: Holding up two options to a friend.

entries.reading: それたかすぎじゃない
entries.note: Said to a friend, not the clerk.

entries.reading: やすいね
entries.note: Pleasantly surprised at a price, with a friend.

entries.term: 少し安くなりませんか？
entries.reading: すこしやすくなりませんか
entries.back: Could you go a bit lower?
entries.note: Haggling is rare in Japan; fine at flea markets or electronics stores.

entries.reading: これにします
entries.note: Telling the clerk your choice.

entries.reading: レジはどこですか
entries.note: Asking where to pay in a big store.

entries.term: お会計はレジでお願いします。
entries.reading: おかいけいはレジでおねがいします
entries.note: Staff directing you to the checkout.

entries.term: ポイントカードはお持ちですか？
entries.reading: ポイントカードはおもちですか
entries.back: Do you have a points card?
entries.note: Cashiers ask this almost everywhere; いいえ or 大丈夫です is fine.

entries.reading: ふくろはごりようですか
entries.note: Cashier line; bags usually cost a few yen.

entries.reading: ふくろはだいじょうぶです
entries.note: 大丈夫です politely means 'no thanks' here.

entries.reading: あたためますか
entries.note: Convenience-store staff asking about your bento or snack.

entries.term: ここはカード使えますか？
entries.reading: ここはカードつかえますか
entries.note: Ask before ordering at small shops and stalls.

entries.term: カードでお願いします。
entries.reading: カードでおねがいします
entries.note: Answer when the cashier asks how you'll pay.

entries.term: 細かいお金持ってない？
entries.reading: こまかいおかねもってない
entries.note: Asking a friend for coins or small bills.

entries.term: 領収書をお願いします。
entries.reading: りょうしゅうしょをおねがいします
entries.note: A formal receipt for expenses, not the normal till slip.

entries.term: プレゼント用に包んでください。
entries.reading: プレゼントようにつつんでください
entries.note: Japanese shops wrap gifts beautifully, often for free.

entries.reading: めんぜいできますか
entries.note: Visitors with a passport can often skip consumption tax.

entries.reading: へんぴんできますか
entries.note: Bring the item and receipt back to the shop.

entries.reading: またきます
entries.note: A polite way to leave without buying.

entries.term: ちょっとコンビニ行ってくるね。
entries.reading: ちょっとコンビニいってくるね
entries.back: Just popping out to the konbini.
entries.note: Telling family or a roommate you're going out briefly.

entries.term: あ、牛乳買うの忘れてた。
entries.reading: あぎゅうにゅうかうのわすれてた
entries.back: Oh, I forgot to buy milk.
entries.note: Realising it on the way home.

entries.reading: なにかったの
entries.note: Asking a friend or family member about their shopping.

entries.reading: どこでかったの
entries.note: When you like a friend's clothes or things.
